projectTitle: Re-CDI Alert: an engineered EcN platform for monitoring and treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
tagline: A p-cresol-sensing probiotic biosensor, characterised with a measurement protocol written so that other teams can repeat it.
summary: Shimen built an Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) biosensor that detects p-cresol, the metabolite Clostridioides difficile produces to suppress competing gut microbes and secure its own niche, and couples detection to a therapeutic output targeting the TcdB toxin. Because recurrence after CDI treatment is diagnosed only once symptoms return, the aim is to shift from symptom-triggered diagnosis toward proactive risk sensing during the post-treatment window. The dry-lab contribution is the measurement protocol itself: a documented, reusable workflow for characterising a small-molecule biosensor, covering plate layout, normalisation, chassis comparison, tolerance limits, dose response and specificity against structural analogues.

dry.frameworks: The measurement page is written as a contribution: seven numbered measurement strategies are stated up front, then each is given its own design, methods, results and discussion, with the standardisation framed explicitly as something future iGEM teams can reuse. Measurements are ordered so that each answers a prerequisite for the next, establishing the reporter, then the chassis, then the tolerance window, then the dose response, then specificity.
dry.dataviz: Nine numbered measurement figures covering the chassis comparison, the tolerance assay, the concentration-response series and the specificity panel, each expandable on the wiki alongside the protocol that produced it.
dry.datascience: Three parts of this stand out for a high-school team. First, plate layout is treated as a source of error: three empty wells are left between each set of three replicate wells, because repeated experiments showed that when adjacent wells differed substantially in p-cresol concentration, the high-concentration wells affected the readings from the low-concentration wells. That is an optical and chemical cross-talk control most teams never run. Second, normalisation is written out as a formula rather than implied, with normalised fluorescence calculated as (sample fluorescence minus fluorescence background) divided by (sample OD600 minus medium OD600 blank), and the team specifies what each blank must be: the fluorescence background from a GFP-negative culture matched to the experimental conditions, and the OD600 blank from cell-free medium. The stated reason is that total fluorescence depends on cell abundance, so raw fluorescence cannot be compared across conditions and only a per-biomass value answers the question. Third, the viable measurement window is established before the dose response is interpreted: a tolerance assay incubating EcN at 0 to 20 mM p-cresol with OD600 read every two hours over 24 hours found no appreciable inhibition at 0.1 to 1 mM, inhibition emerging at 2 mM, strong inhibition at 5 to 10 mM and near-total inhibition at 20 mM, which produced the rule that induction experiments must stay at or below 1 mM so that growth inhibition cannot be mistaken for a sensor response. Only then is the full dose response run, across fifteen concentrations from 0 to 5 mM, locating a discernible rise at roughly 500 nM to 1 uM and a working range of 1 uM to 1 mM. Chassis comparison is measured rather than argued: BL21 and modified EcN (cryptic plasmids pMUT1 and pMUT2 removed and the flagellar regulators flhDC deleted to free cellular resources) are run side by side, and the team reports that OD600 stayed between about 0.77 and 0.89 in both strains with no decrease as concentration rose, which is what licenses the claim that the fluorescence rise is not a cell-number artefact. Specificity is tested against the structural analogues that would actually confound a gut measurement, with o-cresol, m-cresol and phenol all at the same 10 uM concentration, and all reading close to the uninduced control while only p-cresol rose. All fluorescence is read on a BioTek plate reader at 485 nm excitation and 528 nm emission in triplicate, with a no-p-cresol negative control throughout. The team notes a p-cresol stock preparation protocol down to the weighed mass and 0.22 um filtration, with light-protected aliquots stored at -20 C.
stack: OD600 growth monitoring in a plate reader
techniques: Spaced replicate wells to prevent inter-well interference
OD600 normalisation with specified fluorescence and medium blanks
Tolerance assay to define the non-inhibitory working range
Specificity testing against structural analogues at matched concentration
Technical triplicates with a no-inducer negative control

good.publicEngagement: An education page and an inclusivity page accompany the project.
good.ihp: Human Practices is reported in four stages with four named changes of direction. Conversations with a Chinese clinician reframed the opening question from whether CDI exists in China to whether patients are being identified in time, because the physician attributed low reported incidence partly to insufficient testing and clinical awareness rather than low disease occurrence. Interviews with two physicians abroad narrowed the target population from the general public to people with a confirmed CDI history who remain at high risk of recurrence. Interviews at Guangdong Hospital of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine highlighted that antibiotic treatment itself further disturbs the gut microbiota, which moved the project from a standalone detection concept to coupling monitoring with targeted intervention. Advice from a microbiology researcher, Dr Peng, replaced a planned multivalent antibody with a single E3 monovalent nanobody against TcdB to improve experimental feasibility and reduce cost, and also informed the EcN chassis optimisation that improved protein expression.
good.realWorld: The intended use is a monitoring platform for the post-treatment recurrence window in patients with a confirmed CDI history, chosen because recurrence occurs in 20 to 30% of patients after an initial episode and up to 60% after a second, and because diagnosis of recurrence usually waits for overt symptoms such as diarrhoea. Chassis selection is justified against three stated criteria: adaptation to the human intestinal environment, availability of established genetic tools, and biosafety with a history of clinical use. The project also states a biosafety framework as one of its outputs.
partners: Guangdong Hospital of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine

gemsTakeaway: Run a tolerance curve before the dose-response curve. Establishing the concentration at which the chassis itself starts to suffer defines the window in which a reporter signal can honestly be attributed to sensing rather than to dying cells, and it costs one 24-hour plate.
